name: The reprobate mind
about: Men given over by God after they reject Him: Romans 1, hardened hearts, and knowing them by their fruits.

teachings.title: Reprobates are children of the devil
teachings.summary: From Titus 1:16 and Acts 13:10 he teaches that reprobates, who profess God but deny Him in works, are the children of the devil working all unrighteousness.
teachings.text:
**Titus 1:16**
*They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Reprobates are the children of the devil, who work all unrighteousness.

**Acts 13:10**
*And said, O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?*

teachings.title: Agrippa's mockery and the reprobate mind
teachings.summary: Agrippa's mocking response to Paul marks him as reprobate, since the reprobate mind knows the truth of salvation yet rejects it with a hardened heart and seared conscience.
teachings.text:
Festus yelling out, "*Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad*" is a familiar tactic of those proud in their own conceits when confronted with the truth of the word. We see this mockery and derision often, when we speak out for the Lord. Especially when it's done confidently and with knowledge of the scriptures. Left with having to either acknowledge the truth or save face and defend the status they hold in pride, most choose to be scornful.

And Agrippa, who history paints as a hedonist, possibly engaged in incest with his sister Bernice (who is present for this), laughingly says Paul has almost convinced him to be a Christian.

I believe him to be reprobate, based on this mocking response. One quality of the reprobate mind according to Romans 1, is that *knowing the truth*, they reject it. I find this true in my own experience with them. Most reprobates when pushed understand the basics of salvation and Christ. Often better than some who call themselves Christian but who are caught up in damnable heresy. It's a head knowledge coupled with a hardness of heart and stiffness of neck, that brought them to be twice-dead, conscience seared.

Paul expresses the fervent hope that all who hear him come to saving faith, that the hearers be as he is, absent his current bonds, and with that they dismiss him. Agrippa then says that while Paul hasn't done anything to be held, his appeal unto Caesar has sealed his fate. Paul is destined for Rome.

teachings.title: Examine yourselves whether ye be reprobate
teachings.summary: In 2 Corinthians 13 Paul turns the Corinthians' accusations back on them, asking whether they themselves are reprobate, which shows that Christians may judge the signs of reprobation such as sodomy and false gospels by what people say and do.
teachings.text:
Final chapter, Paul finishes his rebuke of the Corinthian church in stinging fashion.

He says he's coming back, and in the manner established in God's law and Christ's teaching on church discipline, before 2 or 3 witnesses Paul will establish who is telling the truth, and who exactly it is that needs credentials to be established. That if he has to come there again it will not be to spare those who seek proof of his having Christ in him.

He says examine your own selves, if they have Christ within them. If they think Paul doesn't, and that Christ is within them so mightily, sarcastically accusing them of not being saved. Of perhaps being reprobate.

This seems harsh. We hear all the time that we shouldn't "reprobate someone." Even when the person is exhibiting the signs of reprobation, sodomy, being a false prophet with a damnable false gospel, many Christians today will say we cannot judge what is in another's heart. But we can judge what they say and do, if not the reason. The Corinthians who disputed Paul's salvation were passively accusing him of being a reprobate. Of preaching a false gospel. Of being a grifter.

And so Paul opens both barrels and questions if they are still in the sins he'd written to them about before, if perhaps they themselves are reprobate.

Paul does take pains to make room for the sincere believers within that church.

And he says, he'd hope that even if he and his associates were reprobate, they'd still comport themselves without sin, doing evil. It's hard preaching, because it puts those balking at giving alms and using the railing accusations against the Apostle to do it, on the hook that regardless of others, they should live as befits saints, (knowing they do not).

He concludes the rebuke with a threat of coming with the sharpness of the gifts he has through the Holy Ghost, but assuring it would be to their edification, not destruction. Again it's a sarcastic dig at the problems in the church while assuring the brethren.

He finishes with a flourish of kindness and grace, and salutations in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Amen.

teachings.title: Unto every good work reprobate
teachings.summary: Titus 1:16 describes Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican clergy, works-based false salvationists, LDS and JW leaders and Calvinist lordshippers, who are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness and whose mouths must be stopped by the word of God.
teachings.text:
*Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled. They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him, being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.*

Every ordained Catholic priest, cardinal and 'pope.' Every Orthodox monk and Anglican bishop. Every works-based false salvationist. Every cult leader of LDS or JW. Calvinist lordshiper 'reformed' viper, with their corrupt modern translations. All of them.

They are rejected of God and given over to their own unrighteousness. And over and over again scripture teaches us to be Biblical Fundamentalists, to cling to God's word, and to reject those who seek to turn others from the truth. Others who, with itching ears and mired in their own sins, can be turned from the truth by these vain talkers. Their mouths must be stopped, and it is by the word of God that we shut them up.

teachings.title: Children of the devil are spiritual seed
teachings.summary: He rejects the serpent seed doctrine as damnable and teaches that the children of the devil are reprobates given over by God, a spiritual seed that does not reproduce but recruits.
teachings.text:
It should not have to be said that the perverted and disgusting false doctrine that Eve had relations with the serpent is from the pitts of Hell and those damned reprobates who promote it are to be rejected, utterly.

Yes, there are children of the devil. They are those who are reprobate, given up and given over by God. They are of their father, the devil. Sons of Belial. That synagogue of Satan. It isn't a physical seed, but a spiritual one, and they don't reproduce, the recruit though guile, trauma, abuse, and appeals to the flesh. And they seek to do his will, and are at enmity with God and with humanity. Murderers from the first.

teachings.title: The way of Cain, the first reprobate
teachings.summary: Jude warns against reprobates who teach the damnable heresy of works and turn liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as the first reprobate and first works-based heretic.
teachings.text:
In the epistle of Jude, he writes of the common salvation, *that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.*

*For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ....Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain...*

The way of Cain is the way of works, self-righteousness, wrath, giving way to sin, and stubbornness and stiff-necked willful refusal to accept the gift of common salvation, *denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.*

Jude is warning against reprobates, who teach damnable heresy of works, and turning liberty into lasciviousness, using Cain as an example, the first reprobate. The first works-based heretic.

teachings.title: Reprobates and the nature of evil
teachings.summary: He says many reject the reprobate doctrine because they do not understand evil, which often looks pitiable rather than malevolent, while reprobate false teachers use mercy to take advantage, as Jesus understood in Matthew 23.
teachings.text:
I think some of the hangups people have with accepting the reprobate Doctrine is an inability to understand evil. That evil, often isn't an outward appearance of malevolence like a comic book super villain. It's often someone who is a miserable human being. Who are sad and pathetic creatures. We take pity on them often, and they use our good-natured inclination for mercy and Grace to take advantage of us. In ways Great and Small. They are the false teachers, the false prophets bringing doctrines of damnation. Who have the appearance of holiness, so much so that they could fool the very elect if possible. Whited sepulchers full of death and bones, decaying flesh. I posted it a few days ago, but the final sermon Jesus gives in Matthew 23 is addressed directly to the reprobates before him. Vipers and hypocrites, Jesus calls them, and says they can't escape the damnation of hell.

Jesus understood the nature of them. It's a shame most humans fail to grasp it.

teachings.title: Thorns and briers rejected and burned
teachings.summary: Hebrews 6:8's thorns and briers are the same as the corrupt trees, tares and fruitless trees of Matthew 7 and Jude, namely the reprobates turned over by God whose end is to be burned.
teachings.text:
*For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

They that bear thorns and briers. Thistles. Corrupt fruit.

**Matthew 7:15-20**
*Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.*

As it is written in Jude; *clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots.*

It's the same allusion, and one repeated throughout scripture. They are the tares. As we see in verses 8 of Hebrews chapter 6; *But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

These are the reprobates. Turned over to a reprobate mind by God, rejected. Their end is to be burned.

teachings.title: The reprobate Jews as whited sepulchres
teachings.summary: Jesus' late preaching in Luke 13 and Matthew 23 was aimed at the reprobate Jewish leaders, hypocrites relying on genealogy and works who are the tares and fruitless trees, unable to come to repentance.
teachings.text:
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.*

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.*

*Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of Hell?*

*Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.*

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

*Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

It is important to point out that in chapter 13 of Luke, which I covered somewhat this morning, much of the preaching done by Jesus, if not all of it, was not to disciples, to the saved, though many may have been present and there is application for us today as believers. It was to non-believers and, especially as His ministry wound down to His eventual crucifixion, He is preaching harder and harder against the reprobate Jews. The holy men, so called, hypocrites and vipers. And those they've made twice the child of Hell as themselves.

They are the fowls of the air, perching on the mustard tree that is the Kingdom of Heaven. They are the leaven hidden in the meal that spreads throughout. They are those who seek to enter by the wide gate of their works and self-righteousness. They are those without the white raiment given the guests of the wedding who came when bidden, crashing the wedding.

They are those saying "Lord, Lord, look upon my works." The virgins without oil in their lamps. The servant who didn't think the Lord would come, and instead ate, drank and was merry. They are the man counted among the share of the unbelieving. The man, given much who received the worse stripes.

They, knowing the judgment of God reject it. They put off getting right with God, obeying the Gospel, thinking that when brought before the magistrate they will be able to plea their case.

They are those who rather than striving towards the strait gate, contending for the faith, that they may be saved to do the work of the Lord, count on their genealogies and self-righteous works and adhering to the letter of the law, the ordinances and customs, but inside are whited sepulchers. Full of dead men's bones. Faithless and hopeless. Tares among the wheat, fit to be gathered and burned. The tree without fruit. Unable to come to repentance. Reprobate silver.

teachings.title: Tares among the wheat
teachings.summary: A professed ex-sodomite who claims salvation by repenting of sin is a red flag, since Jesus, Peter and Jude all teach that reprobates creep into churches as tares among the wheat and can be known by their traits.
teachings.text:
"But this guy came to our church saying he was a sodomite for years and repented of it so he's saved!"

Repentance of sin isn't how we are saved. It is by faith alone. Right away it is a red flag, or should be.

**Matthew 13:24-30**
*Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares? He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.*

The tares, or weeds that resemble wheat but produce no fruit, Jesus warned they would be sown among believers.

Peter writes of reprobates coming in to churches, **2 Peter 2**, he preaches hard against them, calling them *natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption; and shall receive the reward of unrighteousness.*

These are the tares among the wheat. This is the reprobate doctrine, and the warning that they shall creep in unawares, and sow discord and lead many astray.

**2 Peter 2:17-22**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.*

Peter is teaching the same Reprobate Doctrine as Paul.

And Jude;

*Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities...*

Jude also provides a list of traits that you might know them, similar to Paul's in **Romans 1**:

teachings.title: Filled with all unrighteousness
teachings.summary: He teaches that those given over to a reprobate mind are given up to vile affections and over time filled with all the sins of Romans 1:29-31, the traits of psychopaths, and that all sodomites are reprobate though not all reprobates are sodomites.
teachings.text:
*And for this cause* *God gave them up*...

It is rejecting God, His judgment, the conviction of the Spirit, our conscience which is the law of God written in our hearts. The revelation of God's wrath upon sin. They reject all of it.

*And for this cause God gave them up...*

They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. They turn the truth of God into a lie. They worship the created more than the Creator, who is blessed forever, amen.

*And for this cause God gave them up...*

And God gives them up to what? Vile affections. To do those things which are not convenient, that is proper and natural. Working that which is unseemly. And so receive in themselves that recompense of their error which was meet. They get to experience the misery of getting what they want, being utterly rejected by the God who they did not want to know.

And sodomy is a consequence of being given over to a reprobate mind.

But more, they are *filled* with all unrighteousness. Over time and as their twice-dead, conscience seared condition grows, as they become more the child of the devil with each passing day, knowing Hell awaits them, that what they do is deserving death (they know, verse 32 makes it clear), they are filled up with unrighteousness.

*Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful*...

These qualities are found in all reprobates. And many are sins common to man, anyway. We all experience envy, but aren't filled with it. Many commit fornication, many are proud, we boast, we disobey our parents. But we aren't filled with all of it. You will notice the more you understand this doctrine, just how true all of this list is in regards to these dogs. Especially the implacable and unmerciful trait that they have. They are impossible to please and they seek vengeance and destruction of others, with maliciousness. They hate God. They gossip and betray others. They invent new ways of evil. They have no natural affection.

These traits mirror what science of men call psychopaths. They are the malignant narcissists and blank-stare killers, pedophiles and rapists without mercy. Not all reprobates are sodomites, but all sodomites are reprobate.

teachings.title: Preaching the reprobate doctrine against wolves
teachings.summary: He teaches that reprobates are children of Belial by free will choice, capable of evil a normal mind cannot imagine, and that the reprobate doctrine must be preached so believers do not let them into homes and churches.
teachings.text:
And so, we understand and recognize the process. How the children of man are unregenerate sinners, and children of God those saved by faith. And children of Belial, those whose father is the Devil, as Jesus said, are those given up, given over to a reprobate mind. Rejected of God.

*Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron*, as Paul wrote to Timothy.

We can see that this is a free will choice, just as salvation is. We can see the process unfold throughout scripture.

We gain understanding of their nature and what evil they are capable of. And the Bible stresses these things because the inventions of evil that these ravenous wolves come up with cannot be imagined by a normal mind.

We cannot truly understand their depravity and wickedness, because they are not things the natural man can comprehend, saved or unsaved.

It is this innocence that they prey upon to come in and corrupt the faithful. We empathize and we compromise because we can't imagine that level of wickedness, or we are carried away by our own sin. Pride especially.

And not knowing scripture, and not accepting the judgment of God that those who do such things are worthy of death, people open up their homes and churches to these filthy dreamers.

And so we preach the Reprobate Doctrine, that all may be throughly furnished to stand against them. Especially in this month of "pride" where the haters of God promote their wickedness as good, proudly, and call Godliness evil.

teachings.title: Mark them which cause divisions
teachings.summary: God has marked reprobates in two clear ways, being sodomites or false teachers who usurp the Gospel for gain and lead others astray, and believers are commanded to mark and avoid them rather than dismiss these warnings.
teachings.text:
The eternal salute of these saints in Christ, who Paul calls fellow laborers in the preserved word of God is a mighty honor. Their qualities of faith and work towards the ministry of the Gospel are an example we should strive for.

Paul, having called out those he sought to honor to the churches in Rome, can't help but add more doctrine to what has been a master class of Christian theology.

Mark them which cause divisions. Who are teaching contrary to the doctrines they have learned. We have learned the same, being blessed by scripture. Then this command is for us as well. We should mark them and avoid them.

*For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.*

A major theme to the epistles is warning against false prophets and those bringing in damnable heresy, and what is consistently noted is their tendency to be in it for filthy lucre sake. As Jesus said in **Matthew 23**;

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.*

Or Paul writing in **2 Timothy 3**;

*For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.*

False teachers are vipers. Reprobates. Dogs. Swine. **Never** able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Starting with warnings about reprobates, Paul finishes on the same topic from a different angle, and understanding that God has marked the reprobate in two distinct and clear ways that man may know who they are; if they are sodomites or false teachers (often both) who usurp the authority of the Gospel to promote damnable heresy and lead others astray, they are all together corrupt.

This isn't someone who is wrong on some secondary or tertiary doctrine. Or someone who disagrees with you about some verse meaning or whatever. It isn't an unsaved person who doesn't understand the Gospel.

This is the curse of those who turn the truth of God into a lie. Who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Who knowingly subvert and undermine churches for their own pleasure, recognition or wealth, passing themselves off as men of God.

**Jude 10-13**
*But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.*

Some people think that many who preach the Reprobate Doctrine spend too much time on it, or consider it wrong to make assumptions about people's status as a saved Christian, or not. And generally speaking, we should give a professing brother or sister the benefit of the doubt. Carefully and with love correcting them from scripture if they stray. If it is a minor thing, like in Romans 14, we should ignore it and humor them in it that we not lead them to sin.

Given that context, and the understanding that, despite that understanding, the holy Spirit has inspired verse after verse, chapter after chapter, from multiple writers, over and over again in the New Testament, giving these warnings and how to recognize them. It is clearly for our edification. Those that reject it do so at their peril.

teachings.title: Examine yourselves, except ye be reprobates
teachings.summary: From 2 Corinthians 13 he teaches that who is of God and who is reprobate is established by the works done, so false teachers are judged by their fruit.
teachings.text:
As for Paul, there are Corinthians justifying grave sin by saying the Apostle isn't qualified to rebuke them.

He levels exactly his credentials;

*Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you. For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God*...
*Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?*

He cities the work of salvation in them by his own testimony of the gospel towards them. If he isn't qualified to rebuke them, then how were they begotten of Christ through him? Are they reprobates?

And if they have Christ in them due to Paul's preaching, could he be a reprobate?

Here is wisdom; that we can establish who is of God and who isn't by the works done.

False teachers are judged by their fruit.

They don't produce thousands of salvations, ordained pastors, multiple churches planted, if they are not of God. Paul certainly shut up those protesting his qualifications by reminding them of this simple fact.

teachings.title: Normal unsaved sinners are not reprobates
teachings.summary: Ordinary unsaved sinners still have a conscience and God's law in their hearts and have not been turned over, whereas reprobates are twice-dead children of Satan, neither alive in the flesh nor in the Spirit.
teachings.text:
It's important to recognize that normal unsaved sinners are not reprobates. They haven't been turned over by God. They commit normal sin, common to man, but occasionally have righteous actions and are repulsed by the unnatural lusts of the reprobate, having still a conscience and the law of God written in their hearts.

Sons of perdition, sons of Baal, of their father the devil, are spiritually twice-dead as the saved are born again.

The normal unsaved person are spiritually Ishmael. First born of the flesh, born of water  They aren't heirs of the kingdom, aren't sons of God, aren't receiving the blessing, etc, where as the second born (or born again by the Spirit) are Isaac, and so heirs to the promise. The Bible calls the unsaved (such as we were), children of wrath and children of disobedience.

Reprobates are not alive in the flesh or in the Spirit, being twice-dead. Plucked up by the roots and cast into the fire. These are the children of Satan.

teachings.title: Soul winning creates reprobates
teachings.summary: He teaches that preaching the Gospel, as God intends, also creates reprobates, because the truth must be known and rejected for men to be given up as Romans 1:21-25 describes.
teachings.text:
One aspect of spreading the Gospel that most miss, and misunderstand, is that as many receive it, even more reject it, and in doing so, eventually run the risk of reprobation. Soul winning can and does create reprobates, and that is intended by God. Every hearing is a seed sown, or watered, and could be what leads to harvest. But the same message of truth is really required for the reprobate to know and reject to lead them to that state.

**Romans 1**

*21 Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.*

*22 Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,*

*23 And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

*24 Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*

*25 Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: Reprobation is not about the sin
teachings.summary: Whether a person is saved or given over to reprobation depends on his relationship with God rather than the size of his sins, and most people are ordinary unregenerate sinners for whom there is hope until death unless they become reprobate.
teachings.text:
This is why you may have a 40yo murderer, a serial fornicator, an adulterous person, a drunkard or whatever, who, overcome with guilt and coming to the realization of what awaits them, accepts the Gospel sincerely, and you may have a 14yo who has hardly left the house, let alone committed grave sin, who willfully blasphemes the Holy Spirit and rejects God utterly, and is given over to reprobation.

It's not about the sin but your relationship with God.

Most people fall in neither the camp of the saints or the reprobate, they are just unregenerate sinners, with all too common lusts of the flesh. There is hope for them until they die, least they become reprobate.

teachings.title: What reprobation is
teachings.summary: He defines reprobation as a free will condition of unbelief in which men who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge are given over by Him, made unable to believe and twice-dead, with unnatural lusts as its effect rather than its cause.
teachings.text:
Reprobation is a condition caused by belief, and not wishing to retain God in their knowledge, to no longer be bothered by conscience, unwilling to believe and so being given over, given up by God and made unable to. They are given what they want, and made twice-dead.

It is a free will choice as much as salvation, and isn't determined by level or severity of sin.

The sins a reprobate mind may invent runs to those sins not common to man, unnatural lusts.

Reprobate isn't a synonym with depravity or degeneracy. It is the **cause** of such behavior.

teachings.title: Blasphemy of the Holy Ghost and reprobation
teachings.summary: From Mark 3 he teaches that blasphemy of the Holy Ghost leads to reprobation, that some like the Pharisees, Cain and Pharaoh are turned over to a reprobate mind and unable to believe, and that unnatural sin is a symptom of reprobation, not its cause.
teachings.text:
**Mark 3** sets the same pattern we've seen in the other Gospels, of Jesus healing or teaching and the Jews who oppose God trying to use the occasion to be rid of Him. Here, Christ heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath. As we have just read in **Mark 2**, Jesus continues to make this point, that it is lawful to do good on a sabbath. That Sabbaths were made for men, not men for the Sabbath. He is the Sabbath.

Failing to lay hands on Him, Jesus makes His way to the sea, and multitudes came to see Him from all about the region, so much so He asks a boat be ready to help Him depart, should the crowd be too much. He heals the multitudes, and gains more who flock to see the wonders, and glory God, and some unto believing on Him as the son of God by faith. This is important, as He reprimands the unclean spirits He casts out to silence their proclamation that Jesus is Christ, the Son of God.

We see that then, after retreating to the sea, Jesus then goes to the mountains, continuing to preach to the masses following Him. He formally ordains the 12 Apostles to preach and heal in His stead, so as to minister to the crowds that have gathered.

And because people from all over Galilee, Judea, and beyond have come to see Him, and the proximity of Nazareth to Capernaum, where much of Christ's ministry had been, His family, mother and half-brothers and friends He grew up become concerned, not knowing who Jesus truly is. They thought Him crazy. But the scribes accused Him of being from Satan, and the Holy Ghost by which He cast out these demons, they label an unclean spirit. A blasphemy He warns is unforgivable, and is a way to reprobation and damnation.

As Jesus says a house divided cannot stand, as if Satan turned on his own. How can Satan cast out Satan?

And all sins of men will be forgiven. This is important. A penitent believer will be forgiven all manner of sins, but the blasphemy of the Holy Ghost and deliberately changing God's word (Rev 22).

These are direct causes of reprobation that most Christians will accept. The will also concede death without believing is final, and damned. But they often struggle with the idea that some, not wishing to retain God in their knowledge are turned over by Him to a reprobate mind. A rejected mind. Hearts hardened. Conscience seared. Twice-dead. **Unable** to come to the knowledge of the truth. This is the case for many of these Pharisees and scribes. Such was the case for many in the Old Testament, Cain and Pharoah for example. It continues to be the case today.

And because people confuse reprobation, a spiritual state of man, finally rejected of God, and the unnatural lusts and sins committed by reprobates, they argue, that if all sins be forgiven, then there is no such thing as "too late, reprobate." This puts the sodomite cart before the horse.

Unnatural sin is not the cause of reprobation, but a symptom that it's occured. It is important to get that right. It's never about the sin itself, but the state of a man's heart towards God. Belief unto salvation. Unbelief and vain beliefs of the unsaved which can be overcome with the word and repented of unto faith, or rejection of belief to the point God gives up, stops shining the light. The Spirit no longer calls. Three states one may be in, two final before physical death, one final at that death.

teachings.title: The Reprobate Doctrine and the three states of man
teachings.summary: The Reprobate Doctrine, taught throughout both Testaments, describes one of man's three spiritual states, the twice-dead who are utterly rejected by God, and Christians must stop lumping them in with common sinners so they can defend their families and communities.
teachings.text:
The Bible gives us many doctrines that we should observe and put into practice. From the nature of God, our creation, to the Gospel of reconciliation and redemption, and how it all will end, to how to live our lives, handle our marriage, raise our children, run a church, and a nation. Both spiritual things and best practices for our carnal lives.

But one of the most important doctrines, which touches on both the spiritual nature of man and a warning to heed here on earth, is the Reprobate Doctrine.

The teaching on reprobation is one of the most overlooked but relevant doctrines in the Bible. It is taught throughout both Old and New Testament, which not only gives description of how one becomes a reprobate, but example after example of those that do, and warning after warning of how to handle them, the evil they do, and the signs to watch for to identify them.

Reparation, the final and utter rejection by God of those who have finally and utterly rejected His overtures of grace, the call to Christ and the prodding and patience of the Holy Ghost, is one of the three spiritual states of man.

There are the unregenerate sinners, dead in spirit but with the conscience of God within, who, until death, could hear the call and believe on Jesus Christ and be saved. They are the children of disobedience.

Those who call upon the name of the Lord, believing God's testimony and, spirit quickened. They are saved, born again believers. Called the sons of God.

And there are the reprobate. Twice-dead. Conscience seared. Dogs. Sodomites and worse. Filled with all unrighteousness. Hearts hardened, ears dulled. Unable to come to the knowledge of the truth. Rejected of God. Turned over. Given up. Clouds without water. Vipers. Deserving death. Unmerciful and implacable. The sons of Belial. The children of the devil.

Often Christians, who seeking to be kind and show mercy, thinking they are doing the right thing, will completely ignore the final group, lumping them in with the common sinner. Holding out hope, even when they reveal their wickedness in ways exactly as God's word tells us they will.

It is this lack of understanding, as well-intentioned as it's meant to be, that causes so much trouble and trauma in this world today. People who engage in uncommon sin and unnatural lusts, who blaspheme the Holy Ghost, who deny Christ, and lead others to damnation by getting them to deny Christ as well.

I've covered the scriptures dealing with reprobation dozens of times in this channel. The clearest teaching on it is in Romans 1, but the Epistles of Peter and Jude talk about it, hebrews, Jesus himself speaking of the Pharisees and the other unbelieving Jews, and found in Psalms and in the stories of Sodom and gomorrah, and the pharaoh of Egypt... Through the prophets who are killed by these reprobates, and in the Book of Revelation where it tells us of most of humanity reprobating themselves to take the mark of the beast.

We know and understand who these people are because God has given us the information and understanding if we seek it.

I encourage all of you to study on the reprobate Doctrine and come to an understanding to better defend yourself, your family and your community from these people.

teachings.title: For this cause God gave them up
teachings.summary: Romans 1 explains the cause and effect plainly: because men rejected God, He gave them up and over to a reprobate mind, filled with all unrighteousness, not some.
teachings.text:
For... Because that... Because that...Wherefore....For this cause...God gave them up...God gave them over to a reprobate mind....Being filled with **all** unrighteousness. Not some. All. For these reasons, here listed, because that, they become this. All unrighteousness.

It's fully explained in clear terms if you've an ear to hear.

teachings.title: Wherefore God gave them up
teachings.summary: He traces the Romans 1 progression in which men who turn God's truth into a lie are given up to uncleanness and vile affections, so that sodomites are punished by their own lusts and no longer convicted.
teachings.text:
And so, we rewind slightly to yesterday's verses to see the because that/wherefore/for this cause - logical progression of what follows those who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Who knowing God, Who is revealed to us in multiple ways, who knowing His judgment and His wrath, and knowing His righteousness, believe a lie and deny His power.

Because when they knew God through revelation, but didn't glorify Him, but rather their imaginations, their foolish heart, which is darkened. And they worship the creature more than the Creator. Idols. Nature. Rocks. Fables. Traditions of men.

**Wherefore God gave them up** to uncleanness. Because of their rejection of the truth for a lie, God let's their lust dishonor their own bodies. The curse of being left to their own lusts is used by God to punish them. The same as we see His wrath through the consequences of sin and repent, they are blind to it and so He gives them up to wallow in their lusts and receive the wages of their sin.

Continuing the same thought, Paul writes; *For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections*. For which cause? They turned the truth of God unto a lie. What vile affections? *Women did change the natural use into that which is against nature. And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned with lust one towards another.*

So we understand the process, God reveals His truth. Some refuse to see it, and not only refuse (as most people who never believe), but worse, they turn the truth into a lie. And are given up to their lusts, which brings them to God allowing their vile affections to take hold of them. He gives up. The Spirit isn't convicting them of sin, in fact their own delusions justify it in their darkened hearts.

And this is clearly talking about sodomites and lesbians, and transvestites for that matter. Leaving the natural use, to go against nature.

Why? That they receive *recompense in* themselves *their error which was meet*. That they suffer in their flesh, in their lives the wages of sin. That they are cursed by God to fulfill their own lust, and so be punished by the consequence of it. The recompense that was meet, meaning appropriate to, commiserate to the error. They get punished with being queers so they can suffer for it.

Because the wrath of God is a revelation to all men to lead them to repentance towards God in Christ, and because they reject that and turn that truth into a lie, and deny God His glory, and are unthankful in their vain imaginations, God gives them up to their own vile, unclean, not-normal, lusts that they burn with.

They don't "struggle with sin," they are consumed by their own lust. God gives them up to it so they can suffer the fullness of His wrath. It's no longer a lesson to bring them to conviction that they may be saved. God has given them up to this.

teachings.title: Why the reprobate doctrine matters
teachings.summary: He argues that the reprobate doctrine, taught fully in Romans 1, ranks just behind salvation and wrath in importance because it explains the third spiritual state of man, Jews, psychopaths and why tolerating sodomites destroys a society.
teachings.text:
Some Christians question why some of us make a big deal about the Reprobate Doctrine. They say that it's an incidental doctrine, or they deny it outright (having no other consistent and Biblical interpretation that works, given all the clear scripture that supports it).

But, as Paul lays out in Romans, it falls just behind the truth of God, Jesus, salvation and wrath in importance. Romans is a comprehensive theological breakdown of Christianity. The implications and understanding of salvation in Christ, and we are given it just after the Gospels and Acts for a reason, and reprobation is explained fully in the first chapter of it, again for a reason.

That reprobates are the focus of the epistles of Peter and Jude, as well as Hebrews and other Pauline epistles should also be noted as the importance God gives it, as a way of recognizing and understanding just who they are, what they do and how they become that way.

It explains their behavior and why their choices are made but it also gives us incentive to spread the truth and live in a way that reveals the righteousness of God, that maybe some will get it before "it's too late, reprobate!" Before they die perishing or are given up to their own foolish and darkened heart.

It is as important (and tangentially related) as the JQ, and the Biblical understanding of Jews in relationship to Christ, that they are antichrists.

Understanding Reprobate Doctrine as it is biblically taught explains Jews, why they are what they are.

It answers questions so many have regarding psychopaths, mass murderers, pedophiles, why tolerance of sodomites destroys a society, how the judgment of God works on those who aren't saved, here on this earth, in the flesh.

Most people understand perishing, death and Hell.

Few people understand salvation and eternal life.

Even fewer understand the third spiritual state of man, reprobation.

And it is from this ignorance of scripture that the Devil tempts us. It is by getting people to listen to their own conceits and the logic of man, rather than scripture that Satan traps us in snares, leads us to sin and in our ignorance, sow tares among the wheat.

We will finish off chapter 1 tomorrow, and then continue through Romans, giving it the proper study it deserves.

teachings.title: Cause and effect in Romans 1
teachings.summary: Romans 1's because and for this cause show that sodomy is the effect of reprobation, not an unpardonable sin, and that reprobation is a process in which God gives chances first, as with Cain and Pharaoh.
teachings.text:
Again, going back a few verses to keep the context, we see Paul describe the cause and effect, that **because** and **for this cause**, **wherefore**, **and even**... conditional phrases that inform the following consequence.

Many people who aren't familiar with the Reprobate Doctrine confuse effect with cause. They believe what's being taught is that queers can't be saved because sodomy is an unpardonable sin like blasphemy of the Holy Ghost or taking the mark of the beast.

But when we read **Romans 1,** and study biblical reprobates like Cain and Pharaoh, we see there's a process, that God gives them chances to make it right.

**Genesis 4:4-8**
*And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him. And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.*

God gave Cain a chance. God is longsuffering and patient. But Cain took his chance and instead slew his brother, and became rejected of God.

teachings.title: Waters of life shut up from reprobates
teachings.summary: Hezekiah stopping the fountains against blaspheming Sennacherib pictures how those who do not retain God in their knowledge have the water of life shut up from them and so come to spoil and harm God's people.
teachings.text:
Here in **2 Chronicles 32**, and we have the last chronicles of the King, Hezekiah. Sennacherib, a captain of Assyria has come to lay siege against Judah and her walled cities having already begun its conquest of Israel.

Knowing the hosts of the enemy are going to surround Jerusalem, compassing it about, Hezekiah has his men stop the flow of water to the fountains without the city.

He has done great public works projects, and throughout his reign in Chronicles, we see how his diligently seeking the Lord has blessed him with civil engineering marvels (later we see he turned a river to bring water closer to the city).

So his order to shut up the fountains so that *Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find much water?*

When Sennacherib comes, he immediately begins to profane and blaspheme God.

The parallel I see to the Reprobate Doctrine, that those who do not wish to retain God in their knowledge and blaspheme and speak of the Lord God of all creation as if he were like other gods, weak and ineffectual and not to be trusted or relied on, have the waters of Life shut up from them.

While all others are told by Jesus to come and drink freely, reprobates come to spoil that which is God's and to do harm to his people, because they have been denied partaking in the water of Life.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: the unbelieving Jews rejected
teachings.summary: He teaches that Paul frames Jewish persecution as reprobate versus elect, that per Jeremiah 6:30 the unbelieving Jews are rejected of God while saved Greek and Jew are now His elect, and that Jewish antichrists are turned over to a reprobate mind.
teachings.text:
Paul is again writing of the reprobate, the rejected of God, and those abominable and disobedient deceivers going after the *elect*, or chosen.

When Paul frequently writes of the Jewish persecution of the faithful, he frames it in terms of the reprobate vs the elect, because he is trying to show the Gentiles that THEY are the chosen people of God now, and the Jews the rejected:

"*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them."* **Jeremiah 6:30**

This deliberate use is misinterpreted by calvanists who miss the point being made; that Saved Christians, "Greek and Jew" are now God's chosen, His elect, not the unbelieving Jew. And that they in their jealousy and envy, have further become filled with all unrighteousness.

To be a Jew of the flesh after the coming of Christ is to reject God. To not retain Him in their knowledge. Jews whole identity is that rejection, and God's reprobation of them in return.

This is why Jewish antichrists are so wicked. They are turned over to a reprobate mind.

teachings.title: Romans 11 and the reprobate nation of Israel
teachings.summary: Paul's argument in Romans 11 is that the remnant are those Jews who believe the Gospel, and that God does not hold out salvation indefinitely but cuts off the unbelieving, whether individuals or a nation, and turns them over to reprobation.
teachings.text:
Here in Romans 11, Paul is finishing the JQ begun in chapter 9 and 10, as it pertains to Israel after the flesh, the nation, now that Christ had come.

This builds on the theme he has from the start; that all men are without excuse in condemnation, and further some men and nations condemn themselves by bringing God to reject them utterly, unto reprobation. That even with the law, the Jews were condemned and without it, so were the Gentiles. That the Gospel of faith alone in grace alone of the resurrection, into His kingdom, was the promise that faith was placed in. Without works. *To him that worketh not.* That this election of grace applies to the Gentile as much as the Jew. That there is no difference between Jew and the Greek, that if all are condemned, then all are saved in Jesus if they believe. It's flawless doctrine, relentlessly building on itself.

Here in Romans 11 Paul is finishing the thought of what to say about the physical Israel, the Jews, given all this doctrine. What does the Gospel of Christ mean pertaining to the old covenant? (God is a logical God, who wants us to *reason together* with Him)

Dispensationalism rests primarily on vs 1-5, and, like most bad doctrine, isolating verses out of context to achieve it. They say "see, God's not done with Israel!"

But here Paul specifically is offering himself as the example, that the remnant is those who believe the Gospel. For we know from the prior chapters that there is a conditional state to salvation, belief. Obeying the Gospel. And so any Jew who believes will be that remnant. Same as the Greek who are grafted in to the promise by their faith.

Verse 6 has God hammer again the point that salvation is not by works. It is 100% by faith, least it no more be of grace. Because it is a gift and the rewards for work is a debt owed. (Works-nibbas BTHO, again)

So, having established that the Jews after the flesh have to believe, Paul circles back to Romans 1 and reprobate doctrine, calling in mind the imprecatory prayer of David to blind the wicked who reject the truth of God, unto damnation.

However, Paul prays that the Gentiles receiving the blessing and promises, being grafted in, provoked his kinsmen to repentance. That they turn from stubborn unbelief to accepting the Gospel. That they who are believe would be sent, preaching the word, and by hearing, physical Israel believe and be grafted in again. That by his own example living for Christ he gets his nation to want to emulate him and be saved.

This plea is a familiar lament to many Christians. We all have unsaved relatives, often close. Friends, coworkers. People for whom we earnestly pray accept the free gift of salvation but who have hardened their hearts.

Paul's example of being worthy of emulation is a model for us, that we live the Gospel in a way that draws them to the light and softens their hearts that they may be willing to believe.

The warning to Gentiles against becoming arrogant regarding their position relative to grace and the reprobate silver nation of Jews should also be taken to heart.

A Godly nation can easily turn from the truth and be burned in the fire, just as easily as recalcitrant Israel could have a revival in Christ and be graft back in. Prodigals restored as heirs.

Dispies falsely make this an unconditional statement rather than an argument; that Jews **will** be graft in regardless of their own belief or wickedness.

Paul has built his case, in the Spirit, that everything here is contingent on believing God's law and promises, whom all men know, and knowing are condemned without excuse, except they believe in the gospel, which is of faith in Christ's crucifixion and resurrection for the remission of all sins, that this is a gift available to everyone, without works, entirely of grace, but that God doesn't hold it out to be taken indefinitely, and that at some point He will cut off the unbelieving, reject and turn them over to reprobation. Individual salvation to eternal life, or a physical nation on earth, it's the same.

teachings.title: The wicked husbandmen given over
teachings.summary: In the parable of the vineyard Jesus shows the Jews who knew the truth yet sought to kill Him, so God gave them over to a reprobate mind and will destroy them and give the kingdom to others, contrary to dispensationalism.
teachings.text:
Following the story of the fig tree which Jesus cursed for not producing fruit, He tells a parable. The master leaving a vineyard to be tended sends for the gathering, and the husbandmen he'd entrusted with the land beat and kill his messengers. He sends his only begotten son and they plot to kill him and take the inheritance for themselves.

With this not so thinly veiled analogy, Jesus puts the Jews who are seeking to kill Him on notice. They discern that Jesus is talking about them. Unlike most of His parables that fell on deaf ears. The Bible says "*they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and went their way*."

It is amazing to us who believe that there are those who knowing the truth, seek to silence it, even with the Son of the Lord standing there in their presence. Even with the history of the Jews, who killed the prophets of God, and now plot to do the same to Christ.

They wish to not retain the word of God and the truth of Christ in their knowledge. They sought instead to take the inheritance of an earthly kingdom for themselves by His death. They worship the creation more than the creator. And God turned them over, gave them up, to a reprobate mind to do those things which are inconvenient.

*Reprobate silver men shall call them.*

Again, the dispensationalist idea that the Jews held a special place and God wasn't through with them yet, is a lie. They were given the advantage of the oracles of God and the ministry of Jesus Christ in the flesh, and rather than repent towards God, they sought to destroy Him.

And like the master of the vineyard, *he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.*

It does not say He will take it from them for a time. He destroys them and gives the Kingdom to those who will produce fruit, giving God the increase, in His Son's name.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: a national identity
teachings.summary: Quoting Romans 1:18-32 and Jeremiah 6:30, he teaches that the Jews who rejected the Messiah are reprobate by their individual free will and collectively judged, so that it is their national identity.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18-32**

*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,*
*And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:*
*Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

*For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*
*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

Speaking specifically of the Jews who would reject the coming Messiah;

**Jeremiah 6:30**

*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

It is their national identity. By their individual free will. Collectively judged.

teachings.title: Modern Jews as reprobate silver
teachings.summary: Modern Jews are not the descendants of the twelve tribes but a people defined by rejecting Jesus, given up and cursed by God as reprobate silver, which undoes the dispensationalist hope for their salvation.
teachings.text:
Before getting back into the chapter itself, I want to reiterate that whatever else they are, Modern Jews are not the sons of Judah from the Old Testament.

Whether they are Edomites or Khazarians, or some other people, regardless of what Kaiser Sose origin story and Jewish fables, We know they are not the descendants of the 12 tribes of Israel. To the extent they may have some of Abraham's blood in them, So does most of the world.

The one defining characteristic of all modern Jews, and by modern I mean going back to the first few centuries AD, or the foundation of Judaism 400 years after Christ, all Jews hold as their primary identity the rejection of Jesus. Be they Ashkenazi, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, Reformed, orthodox, atheist, conservative or liberal... Every single Jew is an antichrist. And God will make of them a synagogue of Satan.

Reprobate silver will men call them. For they have been given up and rejected by God.

I make this caveat because as we know, dispensationalism is about modern Jews, not the 12 tribes of Israel which no longer exist and haven't existed since 70 AD.

When they say that they think that God isn't finished with the Jews or that all the Jews will end up being saved at the second coming of Christ, they are talking about this reprobate group that the Bible says aren't actually Jews. They aren't even Israel after the flesh let alone spiritual Israel, which are all believers.

And God has cursed them.

teachings.title: Reprobate silver: Judah rejected
teachings.summary: From Jeremiah 6 he teaches that Judah, with its false prophets crying peace, was rejected of God as reprobate silver, and that God judges nations the same way today, especially those called by His name.
teachings.text:
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace....Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them.*

Jeremiah, in the Spirit, is preaching hard against Judah, which has become totally corrupt, and faces judgment from the North, by the invading armies of Babylon which God is warning He will allow to conquer and spoil them.

And the prophets and priests are telling the people "Peace. Peace" when there is no peace. They speak soothing words, withholding judgement, leaving the people with a false sense of security. That everything is fine.

That their sacrifices and their expensive, imported incense, the performative religious acts they do, will offset the Idolatry, fornication and wickedness.

Jeremiah preaches that this is not acceptable to the Lord and they will be spoiled and left desolate. Reprobate, rejected by God.

A millennium after God takes the children out of Israel, clearing the land of the nations that committed  abominations, driving then out before them, and here they sit facing the same judgment. The northern kingdom of 10 tribes, wiped out and dispersed by the Assyrians, and Judah about to be overrun by Babylonians. And despite the warnings of the prophet, none of them repent of their ways. They break the covenant and despite God's longsuffering, His wrath is upon them.

How can we not help but see the parallels and understand we face the same judgment?

God judges nations by their works, and especially by those who call themselves by His name. If those claiming Him, who say they are Israel, fall away, He is going to cut them off.

It is a real 🎯 you are here-moment.

teachings.title: Idolatry and reprobate nations
teachings.summary: Nations that turn to idolatry behave as Romans 1 describes and are given over to God's judgment, as the Canaanites and Israel were, and Catholic and Orthodox idolatry has brought that same judgment on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
*Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the Lord thy God hath forbidden thee. For the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the Lord thy God, to provoke him to anger: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed. And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.*

This prohibition against Idolatry was not only to Israel. The nations being driven out before them had fallen to Idolatry, forgotten the Lord God that brought them out of Noah and his sons. They committed abominations. They behaved as **Romans 1**:18-**25** describes; reprobate.

*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

Moses tells them that they will suffer the same judgment as a nation if they turn to idols. That they will be destroyed, made desolate, driven from their homeland, scattered. This is God's judgment on all nations that turn from Him to serve idols, and even moreso those nations claiming to be called His.

This same judgment that destroyed the Canaanites, ultimately destroyed the Israelites, who were rejected of God. Reprobate silver. Given up and given over to their vain imaginations. And this same judgment exists today.

Roman Catholicism and Orthodoxy especially, have turned entire nations to idolatry, and in doing so, brought the judgment of God upon them. This is why Europe was overrun with Muslims in the past, and why it is happening again today. And in other Christian nations that have allowed altars to idols to flourish are seeing the same judgment, especially America.

More than Sodomites, more than antichrist Jews, people claiming to be Christian yet bowing and praying to idols, worshiping the created more than the Creator, are the reason for our current state.

We are overrun with the fruits of a Reprobate mind; sodomy and abominations. We are being ethnically cleansed. Our children barren and filled with all unrighteousness. And it first starts with idolatry. This is the primary lesson of the Reprobate Doctrine.

teachings.title: Make no peace with reprobates
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Canaanites were reprobate nations God commanded destroyed, and that believers today should mark and avoid known reprobates, keep them from their congregations and urge magistrates to execute God's law.
teachings.text:
*But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee: That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the Lord your God.*

Now, contrast the offer of peace we should make with the average men of this world, the unregenerate, or even the saved who have conflict with us, loving our enemies, showing mercy that we may make a brother of them... contrast that with how God commands the Israelites to deal with the nations of Canaan that have become abominations. Who are reprobates. The dogs. The swine. The idolators, passing their children through the fire. God proclaims that nothing that draws breath among them shall be spared. That the Hebrews should slay every last one of them, that they teach them not to do after their abominations. That they don't corrupt the people of God with their filth and unrighteousness.

Of course, today we do not have the power in this world to slay the reprobates among us. Our government has rescinded the laws against the sodomites, for example. It hardly even punishes the rapists and pedophiles among us. But this is instruction that we may take spiritually, and draw lessons from, even as we speak out to bring the magistrates back to executing God's law.

There are some people who are beyond saving. There are some people whom God has given up on. They have been given over to a reprobate mind, rejected of God. And to recognize them, God's word has given us multiple examples of how to know them, the primary one being their burning with lust one towards another, men with men, women with women. Who have left the natural use, to engage in unnatural lusts.

**Romans 1, Hebrews 6, 2 Peter 2, and Jude** provide us with warnings and what to look for. Jesus taught against the false teachers and against giving that which is holy to the dogs. Pearls before swine.

This is controversial today, but it is the whole word of God. We are to mark and avoid, as much as possible, those we can know are reprobate. Not in wrath. Not railing. But to cut them out of our lives as much as possible, and definitely out of our congregations.

**Romans 12:18** should be our default behavior when dealing with others;
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.* But we should never declare peace with reprobates, and invite them in, least they teach us, or our children, their abominations.

teachings.title: Israel a reprobate nation
teachings.summary: From Hosea 4 he teaches that Israel, not wishing to retain God in its knowledge, was given over as a reprobate nation to be consumed by its sins, the same judgment coming on the world.
teachings.text:
Continuing the preaching against Israel, its people are wicked, especially even their priests, those low men that were established by Jeroboam, when he introduced idolatry to the people and caused all Israel to sin.

Hosea preaches hard against their sins; the violence and bloodshed, the drunkenness, the literal whoredoms and adultery, and spiritual; chasing after false gods.

The Lord says that if they don't wish to retain Him in their knowledge, they will perish for that lack of knowledge. If the priests won't reprove and rebuke sin, then they are in common cause with it. Let their sins consume them. God won't even scourge them for backsliding. They've been given up and given over, a reprobate nation.

They go to the stocks for advice, that is to wooden idols, sacrifices in groves, seeking favor of their dead gods. So the living God says let their daughters and wives go whoring as they have to Him.

What a wicked time, and the destruction of Israel was long past due. Only the longsuffering love of the Lord stayed their end.

The Lord does make provision to keep the evil out of Judah, that the false religion and fornications of the North, the Idolatry of Ephraim, would not spread into the Southern Kingdom, for now.

What a condemnation. And it is the same righteous judgement of God that will be passed on to the world, even as Judah, or that is saved Christians today, are spared. It may seem like the wicked prosper and go unpunished, but as we see here, that is a punishment in itself. Allowing the blood to heap against them, their own sins to make them miserable, even as they compound. And then, destruction.

Perfect is the judgment of God

teachings.title: Statutes that were not good
teachings.summary: In Ezekiel 20 God gave idolatrous Israel and Judah over to strong delusion and statutes that were not good, as Romans 1 describes, while still pleading with their hardened hearts and promising the kingdom to come.
teachings.text:
This cycle continued, and in Judah as well. *Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live*.

He gave them over to strong delusion, that they may believe a lie. He allowed them to see what happens when they trusted their own foolish hearts that were darkened.

**Romans 1:21-25**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

They went to the high places, Bamah in Hebrew, instead of the mount of the Lord, the Temple of Zion in Jerusalem. They worshiped idols in His name and offered sacrifice to them, and ultimately passed their own sons through the fire to Baal. Even those that sat down to enquire of the Lord this day.

*Are ye polluted after the manner of your fathers? and commit ye whoredom after their abominations?*

God pleads with them as He did with their fathers, that His word against them would prick them in their hardened hearts. That they turn from the sins of their father to embrace the truth of the Lord God.

To that end, He says He will put them to the rod. And destruction and desolation. That He will purge the unrighteous from among them. But if they repented not, so be it. The Lord asks one thing of them, stop doing their gifts and offerings and abominations to their idols in HIS holy name.

*For in mine holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord God, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them in the land, serve me: there will I accept them, and there will I require your offerings, and the firstfruits of your oblations, with all your holy things.*

This isn't only the restoration of Jerusalem after the captivity. But a prophecy of what would come.

This is the Kingdom of Heaven. This is the holy reign of Christ. This is the final assembly of believers, who will be sanctified before the heathen for His holy name, Jesus. And we shall know that He is the Lord.

teachings.title: Too late, reprobate
teachings.summary: Reprobation is real and comes after God has repeatedly led a man to repentance and been rebuffed, so readers must accept the free gift of salvation now because the Spirit will not pursue them forever.
teachings.text:
I sincerely pray that everyone who comes to the channel today takes the time to read the scriptures I posted here, and study them out for themselves. Comparing scripture with scripture. Proving all things.

In two different epistles, one to Gentiles and the other to Israelites, God inspires Paul in the Spirit to lay out His doctrines that we may know and understand Him. It isn't gnostic revelation, but God reasoning with man that we may be able to go on to perfection, throughly furnished unto all good works. Telling us directly that we may know His will. And in both books, after establishment of the primary doctrines of Christ, we are given the explanation of the reprobate doctrine.

It is also one of the primary doctrines taught in Peter's letters, and Jude. It is the subject of many of Christ's sermons, especially Matthew 23. It is talked about in the OT, and shown us in Exodus as Pharoah goes through the process of hardening his heart until God hardens it forever.

Reprobation is real and it happens after God has repeatedly led one to repentance, only to be rebuffed. There is a point where it is too late, even if that point is death.

If you do not know for sure, today, right now, that you are saved. That you have eternal life. That you have been adopted by God into the promise of His kingdom, please consider His word. Don't wait. Now is the time. Accept that free gift. Repent from your dead works and vain traditions and accept the free gift of salvation paid for by the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world.

Because the Spirit will not pursue you forever. It can become too late. And reprobates live a hell on earth of misery and filthy affections, until going finally to the Hell that awaits them, to be burned forever. Too late, reprobate.

Don't let this become you.

teachings.title: Impossible to renew them unto repentance
teachings.summary: From Hebrews 6 he teaches that those who were enlightened, tasted the word and were called by the Holy Ghost yet rejected it are reprobate, and it is impossible for them to be renewed again unto repentance.
teachings.text:
Paul in the previous chapters has established his thesis to the Hebrews; laying down the doctrine of Christ and salvation which is the repentance from dead works and faith toward God. The turning from trusting in our own righteousness and towards faith in Christ as the means of our righteousness.

He then further goaded his audience, pricking their ears with scripture they should know, taken from the inspired word of God, *sharper than any twoedged sword,* saying they should be able to handle the meat of the word as they are meant to be teachers to the Gentiles, rather than stuck on the milk of the word, these basics, like babes. And so he begins building upon this foundation to delve deeper into the Spirit-inspired truths of God.

He writes God willing, they can leave behind *the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment,* the milk so to speak, and get into more complex teaching.
