Because, to be more perfect, (which in the Bible means complete, not without flaw as we take it to mean today), we need to grow in His word and in understanding.

 He stresses this with good reason. If they are saved by faith, and so by definition understand those basics of faith as their confidence for eternal life, then why keep going over them?

Who is "*ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth*?" Reprobates.

And in the following verses, Paul in the Spirit, writes again of those rejected and cursed by God.

*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

It's vain to continue addressing those who should have the knowledge of the truth with these basics, unless they be reprobate.

It's impossible for them who:
- have been enlightened to the truth; *Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them*
- That have tasted the gift of salvation, not accepting it but having understanding of it; *when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations*
- Who are *made partakers of the Holy Ghost,* who as Jesus said, calls all men to the truth, *when He is come, He will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment*
- Who *have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,* again "tasted," they sampled it, they heard the word preached, they saw the revelation of God in nature, law written in their hearts, felt the Spirit which is the conscience that convicts us as He reproves the world of sin...

It is IMPOSSIBLE for these people to be renewed again unto repentance. They can't believe. Their foolish heart was darkened. Hardened. Their conscience seared as with a hot iron. They are twice-dead, plucked up by the roots to be burned.

The window to accept the gift of Christ has closed, as mentioned in the previous chapters. Everyone has a chance at receiving the free gift of grace, *While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.*

Now is the hour of salvation.

But those who withstand the call, the rebuke of the Spirit, who knowingly changed the truth of God into a lie, it is impossible for them to come to repentance. They are cut off. Rejected.

*They crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

**Matthew 27:22-25**
*Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified. And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.*

teachings.title: Churches that no longer teach reprobation
teachings.summary: He charges that most churches no longer teach reprobation and wrongly say it is never too late for sodomites and corrupters of the word, though scripture says their end is to be burned.
teachings.text:
The majority of churches out there, the apostate churches teaching the damnable heresy of works salvation especially, the Lordshipers and fruit inspectors, but even many Biblical fundamentalist churches with the right understanding of the plan of salvation, many of these no longer teach reprobation, a doctrine that was common from the beginning of the church as we see in NT scripture, and was common even within my lifetime.

They teach that those showing the outward signs of reprobation, specifically the sodomites but even others, who put themselves forth as teachers of God's word while taking from it or adding to it, knowingly making the truth of God into a lie, these congregations will say there is still a chance for them. That it's never too late. That it is possible to bring them again to repentance, despite the Bible being very clear their final end is to be burned. *Rejected and nigh unto cursing.* Twice-dead. Dogs.

And by failing to teach the meat of the word, as it offends some and is too hard for them to chew and swallow, they stay in the milk of the word, going over the doctrine of Christ again and again.

teachings.title: Our bad report and hardened hearts
teachings.summary: Hebrews warns that saved believers who fall back into dead works can give the lost cause to harden their hearts until it is too late, so Christians bear a grave responsibility to walk righteously so that any rejection is the unbeliever's own fault.
teachings.text:
One of the key points throughout the book of Hebrews is that if we who are saved fall back again to the old ways, to the sin offerings and dead works, to bitterness at reproach, to neglecting our Christian walk, we bring others down with us, who have not received salvation. Who haven't yet come to the saving faith. Who may be pricked by the Spirit and hear the power of God's Word, and so taste of the heavenly calling and fall short by our example. And *thereby many be defiled.*

Especially knowing that there comes a point where their rejection of the truth and refusal to find faith in the hope we have can leave them reprobate. Either in death, or by being turned over to a reprobate mind by God. We give them cause to harden their hearts. To be dull of hearing. To not believe our report.

Our faith alone cannot bring another to the knowledge of the truth. But our lack of faith can lead the lame to stumble, as we bring them to uneven paths, leaning on our own understanding.

Many of us harp on the Reprobate Doctrine because it is an extremely important Biblical truth that far too many are ignorant of, or reject to lean on their own understanding or follow the wisdom of men. There is a point where it is too late for some. And once they are given up and given over, they are twice-dead. Children of Hell, fit for burning.

But this isn't simply for the cursing of those who have been rejected by way of their hardened heart, but a grave warning to those of us who have been blessed by the faith in God's promise and redeemed in the blood of Christ.

Faith comes by hearing the word of God.

So does reprobation. The Bible says they have the knowledge of the truth but don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. That they turn the truth of God into a lie.

If they will harden their hearts and turn away from the truth, don't let it be that we, like David, *despised the commandment of the LORD,* and give *great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme.*

Don't let it be by our bad report.

Rather, if they reject the truth of God and His offer of grace and mercy, let it be because by our righteous conversation. Our behavior. That they see our faith and that we walk the straight paths, and if it offends them so be it. If our separation from the things of this world and the peace we have because of the blessed hope we've attained offends them, then it's their own dull hearing and seared conscience to blame.

This is a great responsibility.

teachings.title: It is too late for some
teachings.summary: Contrary to the claim that God never gives up on anyone, Scripture shows many individuals and nations from Sodom and Pharaoh to Belshazzar and Judah for whom it became too late, and though most have until death to believe, some are given up while still alive.
teachings.text:
*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts...For this cause God gave them up to vile affections...*

"God never gives up on us!" That's a lie. "It's never too late to repent and believe!" That's not what the Bible says.

As longsuffering as God is, He is clear in His word that it is too late for some. The angels of the first habitation that fell in their pride. The people before the flood. The people of Sodom and Gomorrah. Pharaoh and the Egyptians. The people of Canaan who had committed abominations. The Edomites to whom God promised a land to, but they eventually were given up and destroyed. The wicked kings and queens who killed the prophets of God. Israel, the northern kingdom, the 10 tribes therein, bred out of existence and scattered. The Pharisees and Sadducees and scribes whom Jesus condemns in their own unbelief. Judah, destroyed for the unregenerate Jews who rejected the truth of Christ Jesus.

*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, And in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation*.

In the book of Daniel, Babylonian Kong Belshazzar saw the writing on the wall. Literally. Judgement of God against him had been declared by the Spirit writing upon the wall of his feast hall. It was too late for him. That night Babylon fell to the Persians and Belshazzar was slain.

Over and over again we see God reveal the truth to people, and call them to repentance. Sometimes, like the Gentile city of Nineveh, they listen and are spared His judgment. God repents of the evil He would do to them as recompense for their error.

Others, like Pharaoh, harden their hearts until it is too late.

In the end times, as the day of the Lord approaches, the Bible tells us that there will be people in denial, believing their own vain imaginations, right up to the end.

**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

And like the day of the Lord, only God knows the day or hour where He will give up people to their own destruction.

It is a blessing of His mercy and grace, the longsuffering of the Lord, that for most people the final nail in their coffin is their natural passing to death and hell. They have the chance to change their hearts and accept the free gift of salvation right to the end of their lives. But not all people.

Some refuse the truth so utterly God gives them up that they may feel His wrath by their own unnatural lusts consuming them.

teachings.title: No plan B for the cut off
teachings.summary: From Romans 11 he teaches that those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate, and that doubting this by imagining a secret plan to win them back questions the judgment of God.
teachings.text:
And so, *As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes.*

God would that they believe and be saved. He would glory in the older being brought back into the Kingdom with the younger. But it can only happen through faith, and those who refuse to believe are cut off and made reprobate.

*For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all.*

It's all about faith. We are all in sin and grace is offered all of us.

*O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!*

Many find it unfair that some are cut off, they refuse to believe the Reprobate Doctrine, they doubt the judgment of God. They think He must have some secret plan to win them back. A plan B. But the only plan is Christ. And Him crucified. And it is not for us to question the judgment and mercy of God. He will have mercy on whom He has mercy. It's not up to us to tell Him, but to humbly submit to His will.

*For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen.*

teachings.title: The peace offering and the reprobate doctrine
teachings.summary: Leviticus 19's ban on eating the peace offering on the third day pictures the reprobate doctrine of Romans 1 and Hebrews 6, that there comes a time when it is too late to receive God's offer.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 19** contains what is essentially a restatement of the 10 Commandments, and the practical separation of the children of Israel from the heathen that were in the land, both Egypt and Canaan, to be holy as He is holy.

I am the Lord your God and am holy. Fear, or respect/honor you father and mother. Keep the sabbaths. Turn not unto idols or make molten gods, we can see it is the same spirit as the law given to Moses at Saini.

The Lord says that all sacrifices are free will offerings, or they don't count. This is consistently stated, and it carries over to believing on the Lord Jesus Christ, as every sacrifice is a picture of Him.

The injunction against waiting three days to eat of the peace offering, least it be abominable, to me, is a warning against waiting to accept the Gospel.

*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

Reprobation, as we learned in **Romans 1**, comes when the truth of God is given but not received. As **Hebrews 6** stresses, if one tastes of the heavenly gifts and falls away, it becomes impossible to renew them again unto repentance.

There becomes a time when the peace offering goes from bringing peace and reconciliation, and becomes an abomination and not accepted.

Everyone who does this shall bear their iniquities. They have profaned the hallowed thing of the Lord. Their soul shall be cut off.

This is the reprobate doctrine in the Old Testament. It is a consistent doctrine, taught throughout scripture. It can be denied by modern Christians who falsely teach that it is never too late, despite the clear meaning of scripture that tells us that it can be.

teachings.title: Denying the reprobate doctrine endangers the flock
teachings.summary: From Judges 19 he warns that churches that deny the reprobate doctrine and teach it is never too late let sodomites and predators in among the flock, then cover it up out of pride.
teachings.text:
It is worth pointing out that the Levite and his party were closer to a city of the Jebusites, but not wishing to lodge for the night in the city of a stranger, he sought the city of Gibeah, thinking they would be safer among Israelites, to be among Benjamin.

Very often Christians will be disarmed in their judgment by blindly trusting people at church. People professing to be fellow Christians. People who claim to have repented of their evil ways, who have a good story for a testimony, about turning from the most wicked sins to be saved.

Christians may even turn from dealing with an unsaved neighbor, to seek out the services of a "brother."

But God has given us fair warning. Their very countenance gives them away. Churches that harbor sodomites are like Benjamin did, allowing the wicked to creep in unawares, are endangering their flock.

It starts with denying the Reprobate Doctrine. Teaching that all men are able to be saved at any time, that it's never too late to repent.

But the idea that hearts are hardened, ears made dull, eyes blinded to the truth, that some are past the point of feeling, conscience seared as with a hot iron, given up and given over to a reprobate mind, that is, rejected of God, is taught throughout scripture.

In the NT, Paul, Peter and Jude write extensively on the subject. The preaching of Christ in the Gospels affirms it.

And after denying reprobation as real, congregations will begin to drift towards "repent of your sins" heresy. They may give lip service to "grace alone, faith alone," but they will sow the seeds for a works-based false gospel in the minds of the people. This leads to a certain prideful view, where the worse the sinner who "repents," the more powerful the testimony seems in their eyes. "Look who we helped turn around to Christ. Aren't we good?"

And so you have youth pastors and music directors who molest children or rape teen girls. Men who should have taken Christ's advice and drowned themselves in the sea, rather than offend little ones.

And the pastors and deacons who allowed these monsters in will do whatever they can to cover it up. In their pride, like the men of Benjamin, they would rather go down fighting to defend their poor judgement than do what's right, and admit they were wrong.

They will lie and claim it is to keep the testimony of Jesus Christ from being slandered, to defend the gospel from scoffers, but it is selfish and wicked.

And even good pastors, godly men who are saved by the right gospel, who have won hundreds to the Lord, can fall prey to their own pride and embarrassment at their lapse of judgement. And when it comes out, the damage done is far worse than had they done the right thing.

*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: Remaining in the congregation of the dead
teachings.summary: Those who see the way of truth but reject it without truly believing are given over by God to a reprobate mind and cannot be brought again to repentance.
teachings.text:
*The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.*

**1 John 2:19**
*They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.*

**Hebrews 6:4-8** 
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame. For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.*

**John 6:64-65**
*But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him.*

**Proverbs 21:16** is another proof text for the understanding of the reprobate doctrine. The knowledge that a man who wandered out of the way of understanding remains in the congregation of the dead.

Notice it isn't that the person HAS understanding. They are not perfect in their ways. They saw the path, maybe followed it for a while, and left it. They tasted of the Spirit, but rejected it without ingesting, without being indwelled. They never fully believe. And when they reject the truth of God? God gives them up and gives them over. It is impossible for them to come to the knowledge of the truth. To be brought again to repentance.

**Romans 1:21-22**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools*

These people knew the truth, but did not glorify Him. They knew the gift, but weren't thankful for it. Their foolish heart was darkened. Hardened. They were waxed fat, dull of hearing. Eyes that could not see.

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts...Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections...And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient*.

They are given over to Satan. Reprobate concerning the faith. Clouds without water, twice-dead, branches cut off for unfruitfulness, cast into the fire. Conscience seared.

They remain in the congregation of the dead.

teachings.title: Pharaoh as the example of how reprobation works
teachings.summary: Pharaoh hardened his own heart through the first five plagues before God hardened it, showing that reprobation, like salvation, is a free-will choice in which God gives men over after they repeatedly refuse to acknowledge Him.
teachings.text:
"Oh yeah? What about Pharaoh? God hardened his heart! See he had no free will!"

This is a common argument made by people who lack even basic understanding, have their own ideas and just don't read the Bible and let God teach them doctrine.

In Exodus, we see God through Moses, give Pharaoh multiple chances to acknowledge God and repent, freeing the Hebrews. God sends 10 plagues, and at each we see the pattern:

 Blood: Pharaoh’s heart “became hard” (7:22)

Frogs: Pharaoh “hardened his own heart” (8:15)

Gnats: Pharaoh’s heart “was hard” (8:19)

Flies: “Pharaoh hardened his own heart” (8:32)

Livestock die: Pharaoh’s heart “was hard” (9:7)

Boils: “The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (9:12)

Hail: Pharaoh “hardened his own heart” (9:34)

Locusts: God announces that he has “hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (10:1,10:20)

Darkness: God “hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (10:27)

Death of the firstborn: God “hardened Pharaoh’s heart” (11:10)

It isn't until the 6th opportunity that God gives Pharaoh what he has chosen repeatedly, to not acknowledge God when called to.

As Romans 1 shows:

*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.*

That "*for this cause God gave them up,*"

*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient.*

Reprobate simply means rejected. Unable to come to saving faith having already rejected God, utterly and finally being given up on by God. Pharaoh is an example of how reprobation works. The Bible says they are conscience seared, twice-dead, dogs, sons of the devil, sons of Belial.

Reprobation in the Bible is shown to be as much of a choice as salvation. A Spiritual condition. And it is entirely by free will.

teachings.title: Pharaoh and the Reprobate Doctrine
teachings.summary: Pharaoh is an Old Testament picture of the Reprobate Doctrine, refusing God's repeated chances until God gave him over and hardened his heart so he could not believe, and modern Christians who reject this truth accept wolves among the sheep.
teachings.text:
*If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God.*

God tells Moses he will be like a god unto Pharaoh, and Aaron his prophet, to be the salvation of His people, freeing them from their burdens and delivering them to the promised land.

This picture of Christ Jesus our Lord and deliverer, John the Baptist His prophet, bringing salvation to the faithful, free from the burdens of sin and death, given to the promised land, the Kingdom of Heaven.

It is a beautiful foreshadowing, done for our edification and as an example that we may know the mind of God.

**1 Corinthians 10**
*Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;*

*2 And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;*

*3 And did all eat the same spiritual meat;*

*4 And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.*

*5 But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.*

*6 Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.*

*7 Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.*

*8 Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.*

*9 Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.*

*10 Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.*

*11 Now all these things happened unto them for examples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.*

**2 Timothy 3:16-17**
*All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.*

The events of the Old Testament are all pictures of those of the New, that we may be thoroughly furnished unto all good works. Just as all of creation exists as a parable, that we may understand the truth of God, without excuse.

Understanding this, and knowing that Moses is a picture of Jesus, the physical deliverance from Egypt by God's mercy, the like picture as a believers spiritual salvation from sin. We are able to draw parallel with the crossing of the Red Sea to baptism, the promised land to Heaven. These foreshadowings are there to edify and guide us. An example.

And so too is Pharaoh. In him we witness the Reprobate Doctrine played out. We see how there are those who, haven been given the chance to know God and be healed, refuse. Who prefer a lie to the truth. Who after attempts to be reached are rejected, and signs and conviction by the Holy Spirit are ignored, God is through with them.

They are given up and given over. For this cause they are given strong delusion. For this cause their conscience is seared. They harden their hearts to God's attempts to extend His mercy and grace to them, and in turn God hardens their hearts that they cannot believe. They are done, being twice-dead. Sons of Belial.

Just as the Israelites will harden their hearts in the wilderness and forget the God that freed them, and so we're denied the promised land. God decides when. He knows the beginning to the end, and knows who will reject him utterly, and STILL sends His prophets to preach, and the wrath of nature to show them, and still they refuse, and so He cuts them off.

The rejection of this Biblical truth has set at odds modern Christians with the judgment of God. Thinking themselves wise, they became fools. They accept wolves among the sheep. Men crept in unawares. Who have the appearance of righteousness but inwards are open graves, full of death.

teachings.title: Pharaoh, Jannes and Jambres
teachings.summary: He teaches that Pharaoh hardening his heart and the magicians Jannes and Jambres picture the reprobate concerning the faith, and warns believers to know such men so their children do not harden their hearts.
teachings.text:
The story of the deliverance of the Israelites from Egypt continues, and the plagues of God increase against Pharaoh and the Egyptians. And still Pharaoh hardens his heart against the truth of the Lord, given to Moses and prophesied by Aaron.

Keeping in mind that this history is a parable of salvation and the spiritual state of man, we have seen the word of God given to man, through His chosen redeemer. A promise of deliverance from bondage and towards the promised land, a paradise of milk and honey, which is given to all who believe. But there are those who refuse to believe. Who harden their hearts, even as the Spirit of the Lord convicts and rebukes them.

Even as *Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses,* the court magicians to Pharaoh, who manage to stage copycat wonders through their sorcery. Tricks. Slight of hand given them by the Devil that Pharaoh would have doubt, refusing to believe Moses. Even they eventually give up, unable to duplicate the wonders of God.

It is fitting that Paul mentions these sorcerers in the context of reprobates concerning the faith. Those who creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins. Ever learning. Never coming to the truth. Like false prophets, these wizards have the appearance of Godliness, His power, sufficient to fool those who aren't saved, who lack discernment. Enough to get others to harden their hearts to the truth of the knowledge of God.

Paul warns Timothy against such people for a reason. God gives us the example of Pharaoh for a reason. As much as the story of Exodus is a picture of salvation in Christ, it covers the entire gambit of human reaction to this gift of grace given us by God.

The believers who praise God when they hear Moses and Aaron tell them of His promise to free them from bondage. The scoffers in the secular leadership of the people. The mixed multitudes, many who aren't of the chosen people, but go along with them.  The Reprobate, like Pharaoh. The unsaved Egyptians who remain behind, in sin. It's all there.

We should heed the warnings and obey the Gospel and understand the nature of man. Be wise as serpents and harmless as lambs. Watch for ravenous wolves who spare not the flock, and bring whole houses to ruin.

Because, if we don't get the full picture, we run the risk of our children falling to the wolves. Turning from the Lord. Hardening their hearts and having the plagues of the book, God's wrath kindled, and turned on them.

teachings.title: Zedekiah hardened his heart
teachings.summary: Like Israel in the wilderness, Zedekiah hardened his heart against God's word and was rejected as reprobate, so believers must not harden their hearts but exhort one another and stay steadfast while the world goes after strong delusion.
teachings.text:
Hebrews 3:8-15
*Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years. Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways. So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.) Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end; While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.*

Zedekiah hardened his heart. Stiffened his neck. He did not do what was right. And God turned against Jerusalem, and fought against her with their enemies. Jeremiah's warnings, the word of God, had no effect on the king.

There are numerous times where we see this play out in scripture. These people who reject the word of God utterly and are fit for destruction. Who are dull of hearing. Blind spiritually. Twice-dead. Dogs.

They are reprobate. Rejected of God.

But we who believe are called to place all our faith in Him, to deliver us. Not to be as the Hebrews in the wilderness provoking God's wrath in Moses time, or the northern kingdom, destroyed utterly by Assyria. Or Judah in Jeremiah's day. To be steadfast and confident in the Lord.

We should be exhorting each other. Edifying the brethren. Hearing God's voice in scripture.

We should not be neglecting His word, chasing after foolish questions and genealogy. Not placing burdens on other's necks. Not putting stumbling blocks before them. But receiving each other in love for the shared joy of the gospel which has saved us, confident in God's ability to deliver us, even as the world goes after strong delusion, condemning itself.

Pray to be like Jeremiah. Called by the chief governor of the temple who had just violently put the prophet in stocks, and yet Jeremiah preaches hard against the king.

teachings.title: Philistines who would not repent
teachings.summary: He teaches that the Philistines who felt God's wrath yet asked for His Ark to be taken away picture reprobates who would rather burn in Hell than turn to God, receiving the recompense of Romans 1.
teachings.text:
Going against God can be a real pain in the secret parts. The torment the Philistines received because of their taking of the Ark was brutal. Emerods, or hemorrhoids, ruptured blood vessels and swollen painful boils, consumed the men of every city they brought it to. And deadly destruction throughout.

They move the Ark from their own cities to the Ekronites, who suffer the same. Every place crying up to heaven, saying take this thing away from us.

They have the word of God and see the power of Him revealed in His wrath, the hand of God heavy upon them, but they repent not. They say bring His word away from us.

While it may not be as dramatic in our time, isn't this a picture of what we see all around us? People who are so against hearing the word of God, who despite His wrath upon them for their sin and profanity, their idolatry and false religion, that they would rather be consumed by the fires of Hell for an eternity than to consider turning to Him? Reprobates receiving the recompense for their error which is meet;

**Romans 1:18-32**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: God sends strong delusion
teachings.summary: From Ezekiel 14 and 2 Thessalonians 2 he teaches that God deceives idolaters who will not repent through lying prophets, sending them strong delusion to believe a lie.
teachings.text:
**Ezekiel 14** opens with elders of Israel coming before the prophet to hear him, but the Lord speaks to Ezekiel, saying that they have idols in their hearts and the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. They have coveted other things before the Lord God. They are unjust and filled with their sins.

And so the Lord says they should be told to repent, and turn from their idols, turn away their faces from abominations. Otherwise, when anyone, Israelites and strangers in the land, seek a prophet, He will set His face against them. And the prophets will lie to them. And the Lord God says He is the means of deceiving them by the words of that prophet. In other words, He will give them strong delusion, that they believe a lie.

**2 Thessalonians 2:11-12**
*And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: that they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness*

The Lord also says that the false prophet will be as punished as these idolatrous men, and all become a proverb and a byword, that Israel turns back towards God.

teachings.title: Stiff necks and the hated upright
teachings.summary: Those who harden their necks against reproof come to destruction without remedy, and the wicked hate the righteous because they hate Christ and the light that exposes their evil.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 29**, the last of the sayings of Solomon transcribed by order of Hezekiah, begins with the reality of reprobation in those that stiffen their necks to reproof. The Bible often shows examples of heart hardened people, like Pharaoh and the Pharisees, coming to destruction without remedy, despite the reproof of the Lord.

**Romans 1:18-19**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.*

Plagues, curses from Heaven, the reproof of Christ among them, all revealing the iniquity and unrighteousness of men, who refused to acknowledge the truth set before them. And their foolish hearts darkened. There became no more remedy for them, no repentance towards the truth of God. And so they are destroyed.

Vs 2 echos similar sayings, that the rule of the righteous brings joy to the people, but the wicked kings bring mourning.

Vs 3 brings another reminder to honor your father. A wise son will pay tribute to him, but the whoremongers spend what should rightfully be the family's wealth.

Verse 4-8 show some of the ways that a wicked man lays snares for kings and neighbors. With gifts and flattering words, seeking favor. Or by the transgression of an evil man, there lies a snare of sin for others. Vengeance, wrath, or even common cause for filthy lucer's sake, others can be caught up in it when the wicked sin. But the righteous song and rejoice, happily trusting God. Avoiding those pitfalls.

The righteous consider the poor, and turn away wrath. But the wicked don't care. Their scorn for the afflicted and bring others to transgression.

Vs *10 The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.*

The bloodthirsty, the violent man, the scorners and scoffers and fools, they all hate the upright man, the righteous in Christ. Their deeds are wicked, and the good man magnifies the light within him.

**John 3:20**
*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved*.

Jesus warns us of this truth;

**John 15:18-19**
*If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.*

They hate His children because they hate Him. They hate the light that exposes their evil. They hate reproof and become stiff necked. They hold the truth in unrighteousness.

teachings.title: Abusers of themselves and the reprobate doctrine
teachings.summary: He argues that modern translations twist 1 Corinthians 6:9-11 into sodomites being saved, which contradicts Romans 1 and the reprobate doctrine, and that the phrase more likely means other fornication such as prostitution or masturbation.
teachings.text:
There's some bad doctrine and controversy regarding these verses and especially surrounding "abusers of themselves with mankind."

Some of the modern translations that so badly butcher the word, make the phrase into being a Sodomite, or specifically the bottom in a queer relationship. They then extrapolate out that "such were some of you" to arrive at the doctrine that f@gg0ts can get saved.

Never mind the context. Never mind this passage isn't regarding salvation but judgment. Never mind that the phrase being translated only appears twice in scripture, and no where else in any form to draw that conclusion. And nevermind that it directly contradicts Romans 1 and other scripture on sodomites and the reprobate doctrine.

Its actual meaning can be debated, but it certainly isn't that.

Most non-pozzed interpret it from context clues of its second appearance in **1 Timothy 1:8-10**:

*8 But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully;*

*9 Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers,*

*10 For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine*

...where the same phrase is translated as "defile themselves with mankind," rather than "abuse," but the same meaning is intended. They take its proximity to whoremonger to say it indicates being a prostitute.

There is a school of thought, long out of favor, that it means masturbation. Self-abuse being a common term for the act back in the day.

I lean towards this, but it's difficult to say.

The larger context of chapter 6 here, that our bodies are a temple of God, and that fornication is a sin against our own body, hints that it could be any manner of fornication, including prostitution and masturbating.

"But muh effeminate!" Effeminate does not automatically mean being a queer. It means not being manly, carrying yourself as a woman would. Metrosexual f@gg0try.

People will say anything to be rid of the reprobate doctrine and get Sodomites into their church to molest the kids!

teachings.title: The reprobate Sodomites of Genesis 19
teachings.summary: The Sodomites who sought to rape the angels were reprobates given over by God to unnatural lusts and all unrighteousness after freely rejecting Him, as Romans 1 and Pharaoh's example show, unlike the common sins of ordinary men.
teachings.text:
Now, as for the reprobate Sodomites, who both old and young, the Bible says, see that the angels of the Lord, in human form, have come to Sodom, and seek to rape them, surrounding Lot's home demanding he produce them that they may "know" them.

Lot begs them not to, and even offers his virgin daughters to the men rather than give up those in his care.

(This is a similar story to the one told in **Judges 19**, showing again where the wickedness of man can lead.)

We know from scripture that while man's heart is wicked, and left to our own devices, living in the flesh that all manner of natural sin afflicts us if we don't walk in the spirit, daily. If we don't feed our new man, as Paul calls it, but rather live carnally giving in to the old man. And for the unbelieving, this is doubly true. All forms of evil we can get up to. Lust, envyings, lying, fearfulness, adultery, fornication, whoremongering, harlotry, drunkenness, stealing, wrath and railing, greed and vengeance. Profaning what's holy, even blaspheming God or Jesus' name.

Sins all too common to man. We are all sinners, of which I am chief.

And these sins have their reward. The wages of sin is death. And for the saved, the chastisement from God in this life, and a loss of rewards and blessings in this life and the next. Even being taken home to the Lord early, being so lost in sin despite our being saved. Many such cases.

But the reprobate, those who the Bible says have been rejected by God. Disapproved, given up, given over. They are given over to a reprobate mind to do those things which are inconvenient. Who burn with unnatural lusts and are filled with **all unrighteousness**, as the Bible says in **Romans 1**:

*Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

*For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:*
*And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.*

*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

Reprobates have chosen to reject God to the point they are past saving, and God gives them what they want, and in doing so they are now without conscience, and the wickedness of their hearts turns to even unnatural things.

So many people struggle with this doctrine. Even when shown the examples throughout the Bible, and knowing the judgment of God of what they are, how they came to be, what they do, and what they deserve, people still refuse to see it.

We are given the process, the order of operations as it were, that reprobation like salvation is a free will choice. That God provides chances to accept the truth, and they reject it.

In [Exodus 7](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/254) we are shown the process, as we see Pharoah given multiple chances and he hardens his heart to the truth, until God gives him up, gives him over, and hardens his heart Himself.

Jude described them "*These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots."*

teachings.title: Sodomy as the outward sign of the reprobate mind
teachings.summary: Men are rejected by choice rather than blood or sin, and open, proud sodomy is the clearest outward sign of the reprobate mind, so there are no repentant sodomites, though not every reprobate is a sodomite.
teachings.text:
And so, understanding that these are rejected by God not of blood, or DNA, not by their sin (altho there are unpardonable sins; blasphemy of the holy Spirit; altering God's word, taking the mark of the beast in that time), but by choice. They choose not to retain the law of God written in all man's hearts, not wishing to retain the knowledge of the truth that all men know. Again in **Romans 1**;

*Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.*

And so without excuse, they choose. And therefore, as a consequence, they are given up to vile affections. And one of the most outward signs of the reprobate mind is becoming a sodomite. Having pride in their unnatural lusts. Making their abomination their identity. Who, knowing that what they do by the judgment of God is deserving of death, their blood be upon them, they do it anyway. And take pleasure in those who do these things also.

Now not every reprobate is a sodomite. There are some who, despite being psychopaths, and filled with all unrighteousness, choose to not engage in sodomy. They are malignant and damned, and have the potential to do these unnatural abominations, but may have restraint by fear of being caught and punished by the law, by opportunity, or whatever else restrains these conscience seared dogs from acting out the evil inside them. Those wolves in sheep's clothing can be recognized by other means, but some are great at hiding it.

But ALL who are open and proud sodomites are without any doubt, haters of God and twice-dead. Easily recognizable. The judgment of God reveals them to us.

There are no "repentant sodomites." There's none who, once given over and given up, come to the knowledge of the truth.

They may lie and say they have. They may even appear to "clean up their lives," and, shamefully, some may even appear to man as more righteous than a backslidden saved son of God. But they themselves remain sons of Belial.

teachings.title: Spiritual blindness like the men of Sodom
teachings.summary: He teaches that reprobates with seared consciences prey on children as the men of Sodom did, and that as Sodom's men were struck blind God gives reprobates spiritual blindness so they cannot see the truth they rejected.
teachings.text:
Paul writing to Timothy says "*Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron*."

Jesus calls these reprobates "dogs," "vipers" and suggests they would be better off killing themselves than allowing their evil to corrupt a child. They always go for the children. Note in Sodom it was the old *and* young surrounding Lot's house.

And like the men and boys of Sodom, struck blind that the angels may protect Lot, God gives reprobates a spiritual blindness that they may not see the truth they'd so utterly rejected.

As Jesus teaches in **John 12:39-40**:

*Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again, He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: Millstone warning to reprobate pedophiles
teachings.summary: From Luke 17 he teaches that reprobate sodomites recruit by offending children and that Jesus tells them they would be better drowned, then applies the warning against offending others to believers too.
teachings.text:
Luke 17 continues the portion of the Gospel where Jesus preaches and teaches, making His way to Jerusalem. Here, again addressing His disciples Jesus says "*It is impossible but that offenses will come."*

Understand that in the Bible, "offenses" refers to causing another to sin. To place a stumbling block in another's path, giving them occasion to sin. Jesus says it is impossible but that we be offended. That there will be stumbling blocks and snares and temptations brought before all men, including we who are saved. It is inevitable. "*But woe unto him, through whom they come!"*

Jesus says woe unto the person offending, the person laying snares and stumbling blocks. The person tempting another to sin. Woe unto them, that it would be *better that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea than that he should offend one of these little ones*, speaking of the children brought before Him, as we see in the other Gospels.

We tend to understand and focus on the direct application of this teaching, regarding sodomites who target and corrupt children, grooming them with abuse, guile, alcohol, corrupt speech, into becoming a reprobate like themselves. That they don't reproduce, they recruit and do so by offending little ones.

It is a correct teaching to say that Jesus is telling these reprobate pedophiles that they should kill themselves to make it easier on them in Hell, for the added torment they will receive for offending against a child. It is true. The false idea that the Jesus of the NT is some hippy dippy "all is love" God, somehow different from the God of the Old Testament isn't supported by scripture. He comes in wrath on the day of the Lord, and all in Hell are tormented before His presence.

I feel like the high incidents of suicide in the sodomite community comes from this basic understanding that they are escaping even worse punishment than the eternity in outer darkness, burning in a lake of fire, that they already face. Heeding Jesus' warning.

But there is a broader application to this doctrine, one few of us are willing to apply to ourselves. How often have we in our lives brought offense to another? Even if it were intentionally making someone else angry and wrathful?

It doesn't have to be tempting someone to share our sin. Getting them to drink booze, smoke cigarettes, fornication, to steal. It can be as basic as spinning up fear in their lives by promoting that which you know triggers their outrage, and pushes the buttons that lead them to spiral into fear, and wrath. We have a responsibility not to be a stumbling block for others. Jesus' warning is to us, too.

teachings.title: The evil of sodomites given free reign
teachings.summary: The Gibeah outrage parallels Sodom to show the evil of a nation allowing sodomites free reign, which God's law calls an abomination worthy of death.
teachings.text:
*And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel*...and we know, men did what was right in their own eyes.

**Judges 19** begins another tale of the excesses and depravity that Israel fell into absent a Moses or Joshua. Relying on regional judges to come forth by God to deliver them from the results that came from the abominations they fell into.

This channel has covered the story told in **Judges 19-21** before, because it deals directly with the evil of allowing sodomites free reign in a nation.

The parallel to **Genesis 19** and the story of the destruction of Sodom is meant to drive home the point. Parallelism is God's way of signifying the importance of the message He is conveying.

A mob of baser fellows of the lewd sort, sons of Belial, Sodomites, surround a house in a city they are allowed free reign in, and there demand the master of the house deliver up a stranger, a man, that they may know him. These dogs burn with lust one for another, working that which is unseemly. Men with men, laying together. Abominations.

Worse they seek to force it by violence, in a mob. To a stranger, a sojourner. A Levite, of the priesthood.

None of the law or the things of God mattered to these reprobates, not retaining Him in their minds. Their conscience seared with a hot iron. Being twice-dead, fit to be burned.

**Leviticus 18:22**
*Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.*

**Leviticus 20:13**
*If a man also lie with mankind, as he lieth with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.*

**Deuteronomy 23:17**
*There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.*

**Romans 1:29-32**
*being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*
